description: The Somatophylakes, or “Bodyguards,” were a small and prestigious corps of senior officers who served as the personal companions and protectors of the Macedonian king, especially under Philip II and Alexander the Great. Usually drawn from the highest ranks of the Macedonian aristocracy, they were not merely ceremonial guards but trusted commanders who could lead cavalry, infantry, sieges, and independent expeditions. Famous figures such as Ptolemy, Perdiccas, Lysimachus, Leonnatus, Peithon, and Hephaestion served among Alexander’s Somatophylakes, making the office one of the clearest links between royal intimacy, military command, and political power in the Macedonian court.
